output.name: Sekra

anatomy.part: head and beak, the top of the neck
trailing edge of the left wing

output.myth: Each autumn the grey geese go south in a wedge, and the old women say the wedge is the shape of Kael's net. Kael once cast it over the sea for a fallen star. He never caught one, but the cords stayed in the sky. Tavo raised a gale over the Leeward Reach and drove Hasken's three boats past the last rock, and they never came home. Hesk counted them at the pole and wound a line for each. Ennu had shown those men how to set their sails in a wedge, so the drowned gave the shape to the geese. The lead bird points the way the boats should have come home. Its wedge is always a little crooked, because Hasken's youngest steered badly and the goose has never forgiven him. If you see the wedge over the water, mend your net, count your children, and do not watch too long. The sky keeps what looks at it.
output.verse:
South go the grey geese,
the wedge shows the drowned way home,
mend the net; look away.
